title: Proper and smooth compatibility of evaluation comparison maps
statement:
Fix the finite ring $A=A_{E,n}$ in characteristic $p\ne\ell$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. For a separated finite-type scheme $X$ over an excellent strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] equal-characteristic-$p$ trait $B$ with algebraically closed residue field, put $\Psi_X=i^*R\bar j_*$ and $D_v=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,Ra_v^!A)$ on its geometric fibres. Define
$$\alpha_X(L):\Psi_XD_{\bar\eta}L\longrightarrow D_0\Psi_XL$$
by transposing the lax tensor map followed by evaluation and the structural exceptional comparison $\Psi_X\omega_{\bar\eta}\to\omega_0$, with $\Psi_BA=A$. The structural map is adjoint to compact-support exchange followed by the structural counit, as in [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Proper direct image preserves bounded constructibility over the indicated geometric fields. On the indicated geometric fibres the usual localization triangle $j_!j^*M\to M\to Ri_*i^*M\to$ holds for a closed immersion $i$ and complementary open immersion $j$. If $u=h\circ e$ with $e$ open and $h$ proper, then $Ru_!=Rh_*e_!$, compatibly with restriction to an open of the target. These identities preserve constructibility. A constructible complex supported on a closed subscheme is the closed pushforward of its restriction. It is defined on bounded constructible complexes, also without finite Tor dimension, using [lem-trf-geometric-duality-uniform-range]. For $h:X\to Y$ proper, the proper base-change and proper-duality isomorphisms identify
$$\alpha_Y(Rh_{\bar\eta*}L)=Rh_{0*}\alpha_X(L).$$
For $h$ smooth of pure relative dimension $r$, smooth base change and normalized smooth purity identify
$$\alpha_X(h_{\bar\eta}^*L)=h_0^*\alpha_Y(L)(r)[2r].$$
These are equalities of arrows under the indicated canonical isomorphisms, hence identify their cones; they hold for open immersions ($r=0$). The maps commute with reduction and finite extension of the trait, after identifying geometric generic fibres and residue fields. Every bounded constructible geometric generic complex descends to a finite extension of the generic field, and these identifications preserve its evaluation comparison.

For a separably closed extension $K$ of an algebraically closed characteristic-$p$ field $F$ and $q:X_K\to X$ with $X/F$ separated of finite type, define $\delta_X:q^*\omega_X\to\omega_{X_K}$ as the adjoint of compact-support base change and the structural counit. The tensor--Hom transpose of $q^*\operatorname{ev}_L$ followed by $\delta_X$ defines $\beta_X(L):q^*D_XL\to D_{X_K}q^*L$. Its proper-pushforward and smooth-pullback squares are the same two equalities, with $\Psi$ replaced by $q^*$ and both sides base changed to $K$. If $X/F$ is smooth of pure dimension $r$, normalized smooth purity identifies $\delta_X$ with the canonical identification $q^*A_X(r)[2r]=A_{X_K}(r)[2r]$. The purity used is the diagonal/deformation construction [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity], with its construction over these fields; no trace-route purity is assumed. Neither these compatibility squares nor the definition of $\alpha_X$ or $\beta_X$ assert that either comparison is invertible for arbitrary $X,L$.

Excellence of a scheme means excellence of its affine coordinate rings [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: Canonical maps (3.4),(5.1), Lemma 5.5, proper and smooth squares (5.4)--(5.5), with normalized structural counits; Varshavsky §§0.3,1.3.2,4.1.4(b). Local Lu--Zheng PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Use the geometric-duality range theorem to put $D_ZL$ and $T_ZL$ in $D^b_c$ for bounded constructible $L$, for $T=\Psi$ and $T=q^*$. All pairings are formed in the ordinary unbounded etale derived category: $D_ZL\otimes^L L$ need not be bounded below. For instance over $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^2$, $L=A/\ell$ has nonzero Tor groups in arbitrarily large homological degrees. The ambient tensor and exchange maps in the tensor-coherence lemma make this tensor legitimate. Let $d_Z:T_Z\omega_Z\to\omega_{Z'}$ be the structural exceptional mate of $C_{a_Z}$ followed by the base structural counit, normalized by $T_{\mathrm{base}}A=A$. Define $E_Z(L)=d_Z\circ T_Z(\operatorname{ev}_L)\circ t_Z$. The tensor--Hom adjunction gives its unique transpose $\alpha_Z(L)$, or $\beta_Z(L)$ for $q^*$. This construction assumes no invertibility of $d_Z$ or of its transpose. The dualizing objects of the statement are the ambient ones: over each geometric field, the finite-coefficient exceptional inverse image used for $\omega_Z=Ra_Z^!A$ is $\nu_Z^*a_Z^\times R\nu_{s,*}$ with its adjunction transported from the ordinary etale right adjoint $a_Z^\times$ of $Ra_{Z!}$ [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons], stated over an arbitrary field. Hence on small etale sites $\omega_Z=a_Z^\times A$, and its structural counit is the ambient counit [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]; Steps 3--9 use this.

source.place: 1.3.2, 4.1.4(b); agent expansion of the structural counit/evaluation calculation, with the diagonal/deformation purity route

proof.text: Proper direct image preserves bounded constructibility by the finite-type finiteness theorem, which is stated over a field, hence applies to each indicated geometric field. The open--closed recollement theorem gives the required localization triangle. If $M$ is supported on the closed subscheme, $j^*M=0$ and that triangle identifies $M$ with $i_*i^*M$. For $u=he$, $e$ open and $h$ proper, the compactification $(e,h)$ computes $Ru_!$ as $Rh_*e_!$; compactification independence identifies it with the specified $Ru_!$. Compact-support base change along an open of the target identifies these computations after restriction. Extension by zero preserves constructibility by the extension-by-zero theorem, and boundedness follows from its exactness (already part of the recollement statement); proper finiteness then gives bounded constructibility of the composite. Restrictions preserve constructibility.

source.place: 1.3.2, 4.1.4(b); agent expansion of the structural counit/evaluation calculation, with the diagonal/deformation purity route

proof.text:
For an arrow $h:X\to Y$, let $d_h(N):T_Xh^!N\to h'^!T_YN$ be the exceptional mate of $C_h$. Compact-support composition gives $C_{a_X}=C_{a_Y}\circ Ra_{Y'!}(C_h)$ under $a_X=a_Yh$. Take exceptional adjuncts. The composite-adjunction counit is $\epsilon_{a_Y}\circ Ra_{Y!}(\epsilon_h)$, so the mate-pasting identity gives
$$d_X=h'^!(d_Y)\circ d_h(\omega_Y),\qquad \omega_X=h^!\omega_Y.$$
This calculation uses the ambient right adjoints and fixes the structural maps over the actual geometric fields. The same argument defines the proper structural trace $\tau_h:Rh_*\omega_X\to\omega_Y$ and yields
$$d_Y\circ T_Y(\tau_h)\circ C_h(\omega_X)=\tau_{h'}\circ Rh'_*(d_X)$$
for proper $h$. Indeed both exceptional adjuncts are $T_{\mathrm{base}}$ of $\epsilon_{a_Y}\circ Ra_{Y!}\epsilon_h$ after the composition formula for $C$. Thus the equality concerns the chosen structural counits. Composition of compact supports and of their right adjoints, used for $C_{a_X}$ and for $\omega_X=h^!\omega_Y$, is the unbounded composition comparison $\alpha$ of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], which also supplies unbounded compact-support base change.

source.place: 1.3.2, 4.1.4(b); agent expansion of the structural counit/evaluation calculation, with the diagonal/deformation purity route

proof.text:
For proper $h$ on either geometric fibre, use the absolute-trace exchange lemma with $F=Rh_*=Rh_!$, $U=h^*$, $R=Rh_*$, $P_Z=Ra_{Z!}$ and $\Omega=A$. Its composition isomorphism is compact-support composition, and its tensor isomorphism is the proper projection formula, valid on unbounded etale categories. This supplies the proper-duality isomorphism $\chi_h:Rh_*D_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}D_YRh_*L$ with the following specified evaluation:
$$\operatorname{ev}_{Rh_*L}(\chi_h\otimes1)=\tau_h\circ Rh_*\operatorname{ev}_L\circ\mu_h.$$
Here $\mu_h:Rh_*D_XL\otimes Rh_*L\to Rh_*(D_XL\otimes L)$ is the direct-image lax tensor map; by its counit definition it equals $Rh_*(1\otimes\epsilon_h)\circ\mathrm{PF}_h(D_XL,Rh_*L)$. The hypotheses hold without finite Tor dimension: the projection theorem is unbounded, the structural adjoints exist, and bounded constructibility of the resulting duals and images was checked in Steps 1--2. The isomorphism $\kappa:Ra_{Y!}Rh_*\cong Ra_{X!}$ on the whole unbounded categories is the composition comparison of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] with $Rh_!=Rh_*$ normalized by the compactification $(\mathrm{id},h)$.

source.place: 1.3.2, 4.1.4(b); agent expansion of the structural counit/evaluation calculation, with the diagonal/deformation purity route

proof.text:
Fix proper $h$. Precompose the pairing $E_Y(Rh_*L)$ by $T_Y\chi_h\otimes1$, and substitute Step 4. Monoidality of $e_h$ moves $t_Y$ and $T_Y\mu_h$ to $Rh'_*t_X\circ\mu_{h'}\circ(e_h\otimes e_h)$. Naturality of $e_h$ moves $T_YRh_*\operatorname{ev}_L$ to $Rh'_*T_X\operatorname{ev}_L$. Finally replace $d_YT_Y\tau_h e_h^{-1}$ by $\tau_{h'}Rh'_*d_X$ using Step 3. The resulting equality is
$$E_Y(Rh_*L)(T_Y\chi_h\otimes1)=\tau_{h'}Rh'_*E_X(L)\mu_{h'}(e_h(D_XL)\otimes e_h(L)).$$
Uncurry $Rh'_*\alpha_X(L)$ using Step 4 on the target fibre. Its evaluation is exactly the right side. Injectivity of the tensor--Hom bijection therefore identifies $\alpha_Y(Rh_*L)$ with $Rh'_*\alpha_X(L)$ under $\chi_h,\chi_{h'},e_h$. This proves equality of the actual arrows. With $T=q^*$ the identical equation proves the proper square for $\beta$.

source.place: 1.3.2, 4.1.4(b); agent expansion of the structural counit/evaluation calculation, with the diagonal/deformation purity route

proof.text: Now let $h$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $r$. The ambient diagonal-purity lemma gives $h^!=h^*(-)(r)[2r]$ and the evaluation-normalized internal-Hom isomorphism $H_h$. Applied with $M=\omega_Y$, it identifies $D_Xh^*L$ with $h^!D_YL=h^*D_YL(r)[2r]$. Denote the exceptional tensor map $h^!M\otimes h^*N\to h^!(M\otimes N)$ by $T_h$. Its adjunct is inverse projection followed by $\epsilon_h\otimes1$. Under the preceding identification, the evaluation of $D_Xh^*L$ is $h^!\operatorname{ev}_L\circ T_h$. This is precisely the defining evaluation equation for $H_h$, rather than an assumed commutation of arbitrary pullback with internal Hom.

source.place: 1.3.2, 4.1.4(b); agent expansion of the structural counit/evaluation calculation, with the diagonal/deformation purity route

proof.text:
The projection identity for $C_h$ in the tensor-coherence lemma, transposed under $Rh'_!\dashv h'^!$, gives
$$d_h(M\otimes N)\,T_XT_h\,t_X(1\otimes b_h(N))=h'^!t_Y\,T_{h'}(d_h(M)\otimes1).$$
To see the direction, the adjunct on each side starts with inverse $\mathrm{PF}_{h'}$, inserts $C_h$ on the first factor, and ends with $T_Y(\epsilon_h\otimes1)$; the displayed projection identity and the defining counit equation of $d_h$ make these equal. Set $M=D_YL$, $N=L$, follow by $h'^!T_Y\operatorname{ev}_L$ and then $h'^!d_Y$. Step 3 identifies the last composite on the source side with $d_XT_X(h^!\operatorname{ev}_L)$. Step 6 identifies the remaining evaluation. Hence, after tensoring the second factor by $b_h(L)$, the two pairings obtained from $\alpha_X(h^*L)$ and $h'^!\alpha_Y(L)\circ d_h(D_YL)$ are equal. The tensor--Hom bijection identifies the arrows under $H_h,H_{h'}$ and smooth exchange $b_h$. This calculation applies also to $\beta$. Here $\mathrm{PF}_{h'}$ is invertible on the unbounded categories, as are the projection maps used to define $T_h,T_{h'}$: on a compactification $h'=rj$ the comparison $j_!(j^*P\otimes Q)\cong P\otimes j_!Q$ is checked on geometric stalks [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] (identity over the open, both sides zero outside, computed termwise on a K-flat model since $j_!$ is exact), and $r$ satisfies the unbounded proper projection formula [lem-etale-proper-projection-formula-finite].

source.place: 1.3.2, 4.1.4(b); agent expansion of the structural counit/evaluation calculation, with the diagonal/deformation purity route

proof.text:
Identify the smooth exceptional mate just used. In the Cartesian squares for $\bar j$ and $i$, the base-change equation for $\gamma_h$ in the ambient diagonal-purity lemma identifies the exceptional comparisons with ordinary pullback comparison tensored with $A(r)[2r]$. Passing from the $\bar j^*$ square to its $R\bar j_*$ mate, and composing with $i^*$, preserves that equation by mate pasting. Thus
$$d_h(N)=b_h(N)^{-1}(r)[2r]$$
under the two purity identifications. The Tate line is defined on the whole trait family and is locally free of rank one; its tensor and shift can be moved through this comparison, as is already part of that base-change equation. Step 7 consequently reads
$$\alpha_X(h_{\bar\eta}^*L)=h_0^*\alpha_Y(L)(r)[2r].$$
For $q^*$ the base-change equation gives the same conclusion directly. At $r=0$ the normalization is the etale adjunction, so in particular these are the required open-immersion squares.

source.place: 1.3.2, 4.1.4(b); agent expansion of the structural counit/evaluation calculation, with the diagonal/deformation purity route

proof.text: For a smooth pure-dimensional $X/F$, apply ambient diagonal purity to $a_X$ and its base change along $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. The counit-defined exceptional base-change map is exactly $\delta_X$, by its definition as the adjunct of compact-support base change and the structural counit. The purity base-change equation at $A_F$ therefore identifies it with the canonical map $q^*A_X(r)[2r]=A_{X_K}(r)[2r]$. This uses the diagonal, deformation and Kummer-normalized bundle construction, and makes no assertion about $\delta_X$ for nonsmooth $X$.

source.place: 1.3.2, 4.1.4(b); agent expansion of the structural counit/evaluation calculation, with the diagonal/deformation purity route

proof.text: The reduction and finite-trait-extension identifications of the tensor-coherence lemma identify $T,t,C$ and all composition maps. Step 3 then identifies their structural mates $d_Z$ by the injective exceptional-adjunction bijections. Evaluation, being the counit of tensor--Hom, is identified by conjugating that adjunction, and its transpose is consequently identified too. This proves reduction and finite-trait-extension compatibility of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Here reduction means passage to reduced schemes, as used by the parent node to remove nilpotents; it does not mean derived reduction of the coefficient ring on arbitrary non-Tor-finite inputs. Topological invariance justifies the underlying etale identifications for reduced schemes.

source.place: 1.3.2, 4.1.4(b); agent expansion of the structural counit/evaluation calculation, with the diagonal/deformation purity route

proof.text: For descent put $k=\kappa(\eta)$, fix its chosen algebraic geometric closure $\bar k$, and index its finite subextensions $k_i/k$. The schemes $X_i=X_\eta\times_k k_i$ are Noetherian, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, their transitions are affine, and their limit is $X_{\bar\eta}$. Constructible-sheaf limit descent gives models for the finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves of $L$. To descend their extension data use the Ext-continuity lemma. By induction on the two finite Postnikov lengths, its isomorphisms for sheaves extend to Hom in each fixed degree between bounded constructible complexes: apply the long exact Hom sequences to truncation triangles, use exactness of filtered colimits, and the five lemma on five successive terms. To construct $L$ itself, start with its lowest cohomology sheaf and descend successively the connecting maps $H^q(L)[-q]\to\tau_{\leq q-1}L[1]$ using that Hom continuity, then take their cones. Pullback is exact, so these triangles recover the Postnikov triangles of $L$. There are finitely many stages and maps; a common later finite subextension works for all. Thus $L$ descends to a bounded constructible complex over a finite extension of the generic field. Applying Step 10 after that extension shows that its geometric evaluation comparison is the specified one, independently of further finite extension.

source.place: 1.3.2, 4.1.4(b); agent expansion of the structural counit/evaluation calculation, with the diagonal/deformation purity route

proof.text: All identities above are identities of natural maps on the specified derived models. An equality of such arrows identifies the corresponding model cones. The exact derived functors and their shift-compatible transformations supplied by tensor coherence preserve the triangles defining these cones. This gives the cone identifications asserted in the item. None of the arguments cancels $\alpha_X$, $\beta_X$, or a general structural comparison; only proper exchange, smooth exchange, proper duality and smooth purity were inverted.
